question: After the player defeats Tiger Vanguard (虎先锋) and enters the cellar, what elixir did they obtain?

rollouts.answer: They obtained the 碧藕金丹 (Bì'ǒu Jīndān, "Jade Lotus Golden Elixir"). The reward popup appears around 18,210 seconds, after the Tiger Vanguard victory and as the player moves through the cellar/dungeon.

db_evidence.notes: semantic_triples row 0000294 (snapshot_s=18240.0, inside the clue window 18228-18232) reads: 'player character receives reward item 碧藕金丹' (episodes:30sec:000607). This textual caption alone is sufficient to answer the question without any visual sub-agent call, and a simple run_sql time-window query on episodes/event_steps/topic_facts around 18000-18840s (as done in rollout 0) surfaces it directly.

what_worked: The memory DB's 30-second episode captions and semantic_triples already contain an explicit, well-timed caption naming the reward item (碧藕金丹) at snapshot_s=18240, squarely inside the clue window, so any reasonably targeted SQL time-window query or semantic_search near the Tiger Vanguard defeat event surfaces it.

All 5 rollouts independently converged on the same Chinese item name (碧藕金丹) regardless of whether they used SQL-only retrieval (rollouts 0, 2) or added clip_qa visual confirmation (rollouts 1, 3, 4), showing the evidence is redundant and robust across retrieval strategies.

The judge treated the Chinese term plus a reasonable English gloss (e.g. 'Jade/Green Lotus Golden Elixir/Pill') as equivalent to the reference 'Emerald Lotus Root Golden Elixir' (碧=emerald/jade-green, 藕=lotus root, 金丹=golden elixir/pill), so translation-wording differences did not cost points.
transferable_lessons: For 'what item/reward did the player obtain after event X' questions, a time-window run_sql query on episodes/event_steps/topic_facts anchored right after the causal event (here, the Tiger Vanguard defeat) is usually enough; visual clip_qa confirmation is a nice-to-have but not required when the episode caption already names the item.

When the reference answer is an English gloss of a Chinese in-game item name, exact-string matching is not needed — judges accept the transliterated/original name plus any semantically faithful translation of the character components.

Adding extra clip_qa calls (as in rollout 4) can introduce a secondary, possibly-mismatched item name into the final answer; this is a mild risk (didn't hurt scoring here) that keeping to a single confirmed named entity would avoid.
open_questions: In rollout 4, whether the appended '太上仙丹' detail is a genuine second item visible in the same or nearby scene, or a misread from a different popup, was not independently re-verified against frames; it did not affect scoring but is a candidate minor visual-confusion example if this timeline needs more scrutiny.
